sources.title: Same-day article SQL deterministic SQLite fixture

claims.text: The source asks for user IDs for people who read at least two articles on the same day, ordered by ID; concrete schema names are not source facts.
The assumed-schema query groups by user and date, counts distinct article IDs, deduplicates qualifying users and orders final IDs ascending.
The executable fixture verifies positive matches, duplicate-event exclusion, cross-day exclusion, final-user deduplication and ascending output.

checks: two different articles on the same day qualifies
duplicate events for one article do not qualify
one article on different days does not qualify
multiple qualifying days return one user

findings: The repository source preserves the business predicate and final ordering but not schema names; the candidate explicitly marks reads(user_id, article_id, read_date) as a minimal assumption rather than source fact.

Grouping by user and date preserves the same-day boundary, COUNT(DISTINCT article_id) matches the ordinary meaning of at least two articles without allowing duplicate events for one article to qualify, and outer DISTINCT preserves one final user row.
The deterministic SQLite fixture passes positive cases, repeated-event exclusion, cross-day exclusion, final-user deduplication and ascending output.
Timestamp-to-business-date and indexing discussion is correctly conditional instead of presented as interviewer-specified behavior. No production experience is fabricated.
No unsupported source expansion or hard failure was found. Formal promotion remains blocked only by the repository human-approval gate.
